documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group, visit 2022-01-10.

Ms. Walsh returns about 4 months after stopping amiodarone. The cough has largely settled and she is walking farther before she has to stop. She is now on prednisone 15 mg daily. Tolerating it apart from poor sleep.

Allergy: sulfa (rash).

Assessment: amiodarone pulmonary toxicity, improving clinically off the drug.
Plan: continue the taper as written, finishing in early March. No further amiodarone. I will see her in the summer.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine follow-up. Breathing better, cough mostly gone. Prednisone down to 15 mg and dropping, done in March. Mood fine. No palpitations, no orthopnea beyond her usual pillows.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Comfortable. Lungs without wheeze. Heart regular rate. Ankles without edema.
Plan: BMP, digoxin level and INR today. Next visit spring.

documents.title: Cardiology Visit Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group, visit 2022-03-11.

Ms. Walsh, 69, with paroxysmal AF, is seen about six months after her pulmonary evaluation, when amiodarone was stopped for lung toxicity. For two months she has had palpitations, has lost weight without trying and feels more anxious. She notes no change in bowels and no heat or cold intolerance. She finished her prednisone taper on 3/4.

Exam: heart rate 102. Fine tremor of the outstretched hands. Thyroid diffusely enlarged, no nodules felt.
Labs today: TSH <0.01 mIU/L, free T4 3 ng/dL, free T3 5.5 pg/mL.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, digoxin 0.125 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, warfarin, benztropine 1 mg BID. Allergy: sulfa (rash).

Impression: amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis, arising months after the drug was stopped, which is in keeping with its long tissue half-life.
Plan: urgent endocrinology referral placed. Continue metoprolol. Note that warfarin sensitivity can rise while she is thyrotoxic; INRs should be checked more often for now.

medications.sig: Take 2 tablets (20 mg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Endocrinology Consultation
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, consult 2022-03-24.

Referred by cardiology for thyrotoxicosis after amiodarone (stopped September 2021 for pulmonary toxicity). Symptoms of palpitations, weight loss and anxiety for about two months. On exam the gland is diffusely enlarged and smooth, without nodules.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg, digoxin 0.125 mg, furosemide 40 mg, warfarin, benztropine. Off prednisone since early March. Allergy: sulfa (rash).

Assessment: amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis with a diffuse goiter.
Plan: methimazole 20 mg daily. Continue metoprolol for symptoms. Thyroid labs in about 3 months, sooner if symptoms change. Copy to primary care.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen after cardiology found amiodarone thyrotoxicosis; endocrinology started methimazole 20 mg on 3/24. Palpitations easing. Still jittery. Weight down to 57.2 kg. Off prednisone since 3/4.
Meds: methimazole 20 mg daily, metoprolol succinate 50, digoxin 0.125, furosemide 40, warfarin 5, benztropine 1 BID. Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Fine tremor. Thyroid enlarged, smooth. Lungs clear to auscultation. Heart regular. No edema.
A/P: thyrotoxicosis on methimazole per endocrinology. CBC baseline on methimazole; told to call with fever or sore throat. INR today and every 2-3 weeks while thyrotoxic. Encourage calories.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR checked; pt feels better. No bleeding. Continue 5 mg; recheck 3-4 weeks.

reports.text: Bilateral screening views. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious mass, calcifications or distortion. Stable from 2020.

reports.study: DXA bone density, hip and spine
reports.text: Lumbar spine L1-L4 T-score -0.7. Left femoral neck T-score -0.9. Total hip T-score -0.6.

documents.title: Mammogram and bone density results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your mammogram was normal and your bone density is normal too, even after the prednisone course. Next mammogram in 2 years.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in therapeutic range. No missed doses, no bleeding or bruising. Continue warfarin 5 mg daily; next INR in 4 weeks.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet (10 mg) by mouth daily

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, visit 2022-06-23.

Feeling much calmer, palpitations rare, weight coming back. TSH 0.05, free T4 1.5. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Plan: methimazole reduced to 10 mg daily. Recheck in about 4 months.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Thyroid improving per endo, methimazole now 10 mg. Walking again in the mornings, slower on hills than she used to be. No palpitations. Weight up.
Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).
Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs: no wheeze. Heart regular. Trace ankle edema, unchanged.
Plan: labs today (BMP, digoxin, INR). Pulm visit next month. Annual wellness visit in the fall.

events.reason: Yearly follow-up of amiodarone pulmonary toxicity

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonary group, visit 2022-08-18.

Off prednisone since March and off amiodarone since last September. Breathing is stable; she can do her errands and short walks. Cough is occasional. Exam today unchanged. Allergy: sulfa (rash).

Assessment: amiodarone pulmonary toxicity, stable off the drug; the fibrotic changes are expected to persist.
Plan: no further steroid. Amiodarone should be avoided going forward. Yearly follow-up.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with INR result: in range. No new medicines or antibiotics. Same dose, recheck in a month.

documents.title: Endocrinology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: endocrinology
documents.body:
Outside endocrinology, visit 2022-10-13.

TSH 1.6, free T4 1.1. She feels back to herself. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
Assessment: amiodarone-induced thyrotoxicosis, resolved.
Plan: stop methimazole. TSH every 6 months through her primary care office; send her back if it drops. Discharged from endocrine clinic.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Medicare annual wellness visit.

A busy year: amiodarone lung toxicity (off the drug, prednisone finished in March), then thyrotoxicosis from the same drug, treated with methimazole and now off it. She feels well. Weight back to 60 kg.

Functional: drives, does her own shopping and finances. No falls. Hearing OK. Vision: wears readers.
Cognition: recall 3/3, clock normal.
PHQ-2: 0.
Advance directive: she will bring a copy of her health care proxy.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50, digoxin 0.125, furosemide 40, warfarin 5 per INR, benztropine 1 BID. Allergies: sulfa drugs (rash).

Exam: vitals as charted. Lungs clear without wheeze. Heart regular. No edema.

Plan: CMP, CBC, lipids, INR today. High-dose flu and bivalent COVID today. Shingrix discussed, will do next year. Mammogram 2024. Colonoscopy 2028 per prior records. TSH every 6 months per endocrine; next in April.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology, visit 2022-11-17.

Ms. Walsh's AF has been quiet since amiodarone was stopped; she feels an occasional skipped beat only. Thyroid normal again. Euvolemic. Rate control with metoprolol succinate 50 mg and digoxin 0.125 mg; warfarin through your office; furosemide 40 mg. Allergy: sulfa (rash).
No changes. Amiodarone will not be used again. See her in a year.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Note
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Continue 5 mg daily. Next INR mid-January.
